title: Plan born from 2026-05-30-001 dogfood findings D029 + D028
body: Two orchestrator correctness bugs found while deploying the onboarding plan with DontPanic itself: (D029) no_progress breaker trips on verdict-string equality not finding-set, capping volleys at 2 rounds; (D028) audit-envelope filename reuse makes finalizer/close pick a stale higher-index verdict as latest. Operator chose a separate tracked plan (not inline hotfix) because these are governance-engine correctness changes warranting cross-model audit.

title: Land via codex audit-only, not volley (self-deadlock avoidance)
body: This plan fixes the convergence loop, so it must not depend on that loop to land. Each feature is implemented by hand (or claude) then verified via single-agent `dontpanic <plan> --feature FNNN --role auditor` (codex) + the no-paid signed_off finalizer. Mirrors how F003 of 2026-05-30-001 was landed once the volley path proved structurally blocked by D029.

title: Rescope after failed implementation: diminishing_returns and precedence are in scope
body: The first implementation attempt failed because the draft plan encoded a faulty assumption: check_diminishing_returns was described as already correct and the non_goals effectively excluded the real convergence blocker. The actual failure mode includes diminishing_returns false positives and/or supervisor breaker precedence terminating progress-making rounds before max_iterations/signoff. This draft is amended before re-lock/re-dispatch: F001 now covers no_progress, diminishing_returns, and the minimum breaker ordering/precedence needed to keep shrinking/changing finding sets alive; objective_contract non_goals are narrowed to exclude unrelated breaker rewrites only. D028 stale-envelope selection remains independently valid.

title: One batched codex audit for F001+F002+F003 (one-paid-call budget)
body: Operator chose a single batched codex auditor invocation covering all three features rather than D002's per-feature auditor (which would be 3 paid calls). Budget locked at EXACTLY ONE live codex exec call (read-only sandbox, model gpt-5.5). The single call reviews the three commit diffs (b9b2b10 F001, 950bfe1 F002, 2699cb1 F003) against objective_contract.json + the full-sweep evidence and returns a per-feature verdict. On signed_off the per-feature no-paid finalizer (signed_off_finalizer) flips each passes:true — its guards independently re-read the verdict, so the batched-envelope materialization cannot bypass the signoff requirement. A second live call requires explicit operator approval (cf. one-paid-call-dogfood-discipline).

title: Codex batched audit reconciliation: F001/F003 acceptance text was stale vs Design B (code correct)
body: The single batched codex audit (D004; evidence/codex-batched-audit-i0.json, model gpt-5.5) returned overall needs_changes: F002 signed_off; F001+F003 needs_changes. All three F001/F003 findings reduce to ONE root cause — the F001/F003 acceptance text still said 'no_progress trips only when the signature SET is identical' and 'diminishing_returns treats changing sets as progress', but Design B (D003, operator-approved) deliberately implements the NARROWER 'strictly-shrinking COUNT = progress; flat-changed ({A}->{B}) and growing ({A}->{A,B}) still terminate'. The code is correct on the merits: growing findings are a regression (must stop), and flat-distinct findings are the pre-existing thrashing case that plan 2026-05-04-003's test_legitimate_no_progress_still_terminates_stopped_no_progress intentionally terminates — broadening no_progress to identical-set-only would BREAK that regression contract. Classified per volley-failure-taxonomy as interpretive_disagreement / spec-clarification, NOT feature_defect. Resolution (operator decision): acceptance text for F001/F003 updated to describe Design B accurately; no code change; no second paid call. F002 was independently codex-signed_off. All three flipped passes:true as operator-accepted. The engine behaved correctly end-to-end — codex returned needs_changes so the no-paid signed_off finalizer would have refused (exit 3); the close here is a documented operator override at the governance layer, not a silent finalize.
